articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.summary: Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary: Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

articles.title: Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a way to operate multiple silicon qubits simultaneously with remarkable accuracy, overcoming a major challenge in scaling up quantum computers. Their new technique maintained accuracy of approximately 99.9% even when all five qubits were running at once, opening the door to larger and more powerful quantum processors.

articles.title: Superhuman pushes its Go assistant everywhere
articles.summary: Superhuman is making Go its central agent and making it available in Docs and Mail

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.

articles.title: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
articles.summary: The Microsoft CEO downplayed the recent Outlook outage while noting that AI was causing both opportunities and new challenges for securing much of the connected world.

articles.title: Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like ‘kicking Michael Jordan off your team’
articles.summary: “I don’t think [Huang is] disloyal to the United States," Musk said.

With this change, you can disable the graphic design platform's array of AI tools, such as its AI photo-extending Magic Expand feature, as well as turn off the ability to generate images with its Canva chatbot. This toggle doesn't turn off every AI-powered […]

articles.summary: President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. articles.title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
articles.summary: With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits. On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online […]

articles.title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI
articles.summary: As advanced and lifelike as the animatronic characters at Disney parks have become, they typically either stick to predefined movements and routines, or there's an out of sight puppeteer helping make their behavior appear more spontaneous. That could soon change as Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has revealed three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes that rely on Amazon's […]

articles.title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either
articles.summary: This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used […]

articles.title: Will Wright’s next game uses AI to map your memories
articles.summary: Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims, is working on a new game - and it's built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems. Like Wright's other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. […]

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.

articles.title: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
articles.summary: Scientists have filmed tiny magnetic vortices called skyrmions melting out of an organized lattice for the first time, revealing new ways to manipulate these unusual structures. The breakthrough could help make brain-like computers a reality, potentially enabling dramatically smaller and more energy-efficient technology.

articles.title: A little manganese makes a big difference for next-generation batteries
articles.summary: As electric vehicles become more widespread, researchers are looking for ways to make rechargeable batteries store more energy while reducing their cost and environmental impact. Aluminum is a promising candidate. It can store large amounts of lithium, and a single sheet of aluminum foil can serve as both the battery's active material and the component that carries electricity.

articles.title: AI helps uncover critical flaw in ubiquitous internet software
articles.summary: If you checked your bank balance, booked a flight or ordered groceries online today, there is a good chance your request was handled by a computer program written in Java.

articles.title: New framework guides defense software upgrades by mapping risks and operational constraints
articles.summary: Modernizing aging software is a challenge for any organization. But for defense programs that depend on complex technology to support critical operations, the stakes are particularly high. Legacy systems often support ongoing operations, some critical to national security and other government functions, that cannot be paused for an upgrade.

articles.title: Three studies examine how autonomous AI reshapes responsibility, expertise and real-world decisions
articles.summary: Who is responsible for the actions of an autonomous artificial system, how much authority should be attributed to its judgments, and what changes when it acts in the physical world? The public and scientific debate on artificial intelligence is increasingly focusing on agentic AI (or Agentic AI), namely systems capable of pursuing goals and autonomously deciding which actions to take to achieve them, without requiring human intervention at every step.

articles.title: Insights into data center resource use in Nevada
articles.summary: With the rapid proliferation of the digital realm and a growing artificial intelligence sector, data centers are spreading across the world. Nevada is one of the fastest-growing data center regions in the U.S. and globally due to abundant land, cost-competitive energy and an attractive tax and regulatory environment. This explosive growth offers both opportunities and challenges due to the water and electricity required to operate these centers.

articles.title: Who gets Europe's scrap? Industry fights over future of waste exports
articles.summary: A fight over scrap metal is pitting recyclers against manufacturers, with India and Egypt lobbying to keep buying metric tons of it from Europe to be melted down and reused.

articles.title: Old infrastructure, AI-driven fixes behind wave of US outages
articles.summary: A sudden spate of disruptive tech breakdowns in the United States has triggered widespread public unease and compelled top officials to counter rampant speculation about everything from malicious actors to unchecked AI.

articles.title: China's used phones find new homes from Karachi to Algiers
articles.summary: In the maze of Shenzhen's neon-lit Huaqiangbei electronics market, buyers from Africa to Bangladesh buy dozens of used phones at a time—even with cracked screens—to sell back home.

articles.title: Tech outages are piling up, and AI is raising the stakes. Could this be the new normal?
articles.summary: Inaccessible email inboxes. Banking delays. And a communications meltdown that grounded airplanes for hours, followed by waves of other travel disruptions.
